{{Quote|The power to destroy life is at your command!|The Presence to Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />}}
The '''Presence''' was a [[Gender|female]] [[Sith]] who once commanded the [[Malachor superweapon|weapon]] on the [[Malachor Sith Temple|Sith temple]] on the [[planet]] [[Malachor]]. In [[3 BBY]], her voice was heard by [[Ezra Bridger]] when he used a [[Sith holocron]] to inadvertently activate the superweapon. Bridger was led by the former [[Sith Lord]] once known as [[Maul|Darth Maul]] to believe that using the [[holocron]] would grant him the knowledge he needed to destroy the [[Sith]]. Once he activated the temple however, the Presence told him that the knowledge contained within the holocron was the power of the temple's [[battle station]] and that it had the power to destroy life.

==Biography==
The Presence was a [[Gender|female]] [[Sith]] who, prior to<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> [[3 BBY]],<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Twilight of the Apprentice]]" to [[3 BBY]].</ref> once commanded the [[Malachor superweapon|weapon]] on the [[Malachor Sith Temple|Sith temple]] on the desolate [[planet]] [[Malachor]]. Eventually her voice became confined to a [[Sith holocron (Malachor)|Sith holocron]].<ref name="BMF 96">{{BuildFalconCite|96|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref>

In 3 BBY,<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice Date" /> [[Padawan]] [[Ezra Bridger]] and his master, [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]], [[Mission to Malachor|traveled]] with former [[Jedi]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] to Malachor to find ancient Sith knowledge, which they hoped to use to defeat the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and his [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]]. On Malachor, Bridger encountered the former Sith Lord once known as [[Maul|Darth Maul]], who also sought the secrets of the [[Malachor Sith Temple|Sith temple]]. The two worked together to enter the [[Sith temple|temple]] and ultimately retrieved a [[Sith holocron]], which Maul said would unlock the temple's secret knowledge. Bridger was sent to the top of the temple alone, where Maul told him to activate the temple.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />

[[File:EzraSithHolocron.png|thumb|right|280px|Ezra activated the temple with the holocron, afterwards speaking to Presence.]]
Bridger reached the top of the temple, where the [[holocron]] levitated out of his hand and entered an obelisk. Its activation set off currents of electricity, and the female voice of the Presence asked Bridger who he was. Bridger explained that he sought the knowledge of the temple to defeat his enemies, and the Presence told him that knowledge is power. The temple, which in truth was an ancient [[battle station]], activated its [[superweapon]] and the Presence told Bridger that the power to destroy life was at his command. Bridger said he did not want that power, so the Presence said the other who had arrived at the temple might—[[Darth]] Vader. As Vader [[Lightsaber duel|dueled]] Tano, Bridger and Jarrus worked together to remove the holocron from the obelisk and deactivate the weapon. With the holocron in hand, the two Jedi were forced to flee Malachor without Tano, as she and Vader were sealed within the temple dueling one another as the temple collapsed.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />

Over the next six [[Standard month|months]],<ref name="Steps Trivia">{{SW|url=episodes/steps-into-shadow-trivia-gallery|text="Steps Into Shadow" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> Bridger regularly made use of the knowledge within the holocron and speak to the Presence, as she seduced him closer and closer to the [[dark side of the Force]]. After undertaking a mission to [[Rescue of Hondo Ohnaka|rescue]] the [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] from [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Prison|custody]], Bridger returned to his quarters, expressing frustration at being blamed for failing to acquire all the details of the mission. Bridger opened the holocron once more and spoke with the Presence, who told him that his anger would make him more powerful and more focused. Jarrus, however, soon discovered the holocron in Bridger's quarters and took it from him, later giving it to [[Bendu]] as a gift after their meeting.<ref name="Steps">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Presence appeared as a voice in "[[Twilight of the Apprentice]]," the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Two|second season]] finale of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. She was voiced by [[Nika Futterman]].<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />

In an interview with [[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]] that was posted after the episode aired, series executive producer [[Dave Filoni]] provided some insight into what he saw as the backstory of the Presence. In his mind, the voice of the Presence is the voice of the ancient Sith Lord who built the Malachor temple. Filoni said that he liked the idea of an ancient and powerful woman, who had domination that the audience has not yet heard of, who was creating the weapon when it was [[Great Scourge of Malachor|attacked]] by the [[Jedi Order]] and everyone was turned to stone. Filoni further said that he has a name for the character, but he could not yet reveal it.<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://uk.ign.com/articles/2016/03/31/star-wars-rebels-dave-filoni-on-ahsokas-fate-mauls-return-and-much-more?page=1|text=''Star Wars Rebels'': Dave Filoni on Ahsoka's Fate, Maul's Return and Much More|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2016-03-30|work=IGN|archivedate=20200103221540}}</ref> She is identified solely as "Presence" in the episode's credits.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />

The [[2018]] sourcebook ''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' mentions a [[Unidentified Sith witch|Sith witch]] who led Sith military forces during the Great Scourge of Malachor, the battle in which the superweapon was activated and misfired.<ref name="DOR">''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]''</ref> The [[2019]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' identifies the Sith Lord who constructed the Malachor superweapon as [[Darth Tanis]].<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Any potential correlation between the three characters has not been confirmed by any [[canon]] source.
